findings.title: (1) Target guard confirmed live at HEAD — protects the save's fresh re-read
findings.detail: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:1724 (on main, HEAD e6fab8b): `if (!routeLoad.isCurrent(g) || recordEditorMemberId !== memberId) return;` — text matches the issue's citation verbatim. It sits immediately after `const fresh = await loadMemberRecord(cfg, row.personId);` at :1718, inside `saveRecordEditor`'s try block. The generation is captured just above at :1704 (`const g = routeLoad.generation;`), right before `recordSavingMemberId = memberId;` and the try. So the guard protects the SAVE-TIME re-read (not the editor-open read at openRecordEditor's own loadMemberRecord call, which is a separate call site with its own separate guard at :1552). Comment at :1712-1717 spells out exactly the race this guard closes: 'a collective switch, the admin opening another row' across the re-read await.

findings.title: (2) Issue's ':732' citation is off by one test — the actual held-promise pin is at :742, and it holds createMemberRecord, not loadMemberRecord
findings.detail: main:src/routes/page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts. Line 732 (`it('a collective switch mid-edit CLOSES...')`) is the SIMPLE close test — no held promise at all. The held-promise machinery the issue is pointing at is the NEXT test, `it('a held save SUCCESS settling after the switch writes NOTHING...')`, which starts at :742 and runs to :758. Its machinery: `let release!: () => void; createMemberRecordMock.mockImplementation(() => new Promise<string>((res) => (release = () => res('rec-new'))));` (743-745) — defers the CREATE call's resolution (i.e. holds the write itself, not the fresh re-read before it). Flow: `renderTwoCollectivesAsAdmin()` -> `openEditor(m2)` -> click save -> `await tick()` (lets the click handler run through to the held create) -> `selectedCollectiveDbStore.set('other-choir')` -> `waitFor` row gone -> `release()` -> `flush()+tick()` -> assert status text empty and editor closed. This exercises the POST-write guard at :1777 ('superseded — write nothing'), not the pre-write guard at :1724 that #279 targets. The new pin should mirror this shape (render-two-collectives helper, open editor, click save, tick, switch, release, flush+tick, assert) but move the held promise one step earlier onto `loadMemberRecordMock`'s SECOND call instead of `createMemberRecordMock`.

findings.title: (3) Collective-switch helper exists and is reusable as-is
findings.detail: `renderTwoCollectivesAsAdmin()` (main:src/routes/page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts:719-730) plus `setAuthedWithTwoCollectives()` (:151) and the `selectedCollectiveDbStore` import (:129) are already in the file and already used by the two existing tests in the `(E) collective switch — #259 generation discipline` describe block (:718-759). The new pin needs no new helper — it can call `renderTwoCollectivesAsAdmin()`, `openEditor(container, 'm2')`, then `selectedCollectiveDbStore.set('other-choir')` exactly like the :742 test does.

findings.title: (4) Stale title confirmed — current line is :324, not :317, and the parenthetical is now false
findings.detail: main:src/routes/page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts:324: `it('opening runs the ONE record lookup for that member (check-then-create + editor load share the query)', ...)`. The test body (:324-332) only clicks through `openEditor` and asserts `loadMemberRecordMock` was called exactly once with the row's personId — it never touches save at all, so it can't be asserting anything about a SHARED query with check-then-create. Confirmed false via the code: commit 0d1af3d ('fix(#268): ... existence check moves to the save (review YELLOW r3)', 2026-09-07) moved the one-record-per-person check OUT of `openRecordEditor` and INTO `saveRecordEditor`'s own fresh `loadMemberRecord` call (now :1718) — its commit message states explicitly: 'The one-record-per-person check moved from editor-open into the write. saveRecordEditor re-reads the record with loadMemberRecord ... so a create can no longer fire on a stale lookup.' So today there are two independent `loadMemberRecord` call sites (open-time :1552-area, save-time :1718) rather than one shared query — the parenthetical is stale/false, exactly as the issue claims.

findings.title: (5) The proposed pin does discriminate guarded vs unguarded — reasoned through both branches
findings.detail: Proposed pin (per issue body): sequence `loadMemberRecordMock.mockResolvedValueOnce({state:'none'})` (consumed by openEditor's read) then `.mockImplementationOnce(() => new Promise(res => release = res))` (consumed by saveRecordEditor's fresh re-read at :1718) on top of the default row m2 (name 'Berta Bass', email 'berta@example.com' — both fixture-valid per main:src/routes/page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts:172 — so the three validation gates before the generation capture all pass cleanly, matching the pattern already proven by the :742 test on the same row). Timeline: open editor (call 1 resolves 'none', prefills form) -> click save -> tick() lets execution reach and suspend on the held call 2 -> switch collective (bumps `routeLoad.generation` AND, via `reset()` at :240, nulls `recordEditorMemberId`) -> release({state:'none'}) -> flush+tick resumes saveRecordEditor after `const fresh = await loadMemberRecord(...)`.  WITH the guard at :1724 present: `!routeLoad.isCurrent(g)` is true (generation bumped) -> early return -> `createMemberRecordMock`/`updateMemberRecordMock` never called -> both `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` assertions pass. WITH the guard line deleted: execution falls through to `if (fresh.state === 'none')` (true, since released value is `{state:'none'}`) -> calls `createMemberRecord(cfg, {...})` using the closed-over `cfg`/`row` (still resolvable — `row.dbEntityId` is 'db-1' from the fixture, so the `dbEntityId` null-check at that branch doesn't throw either) -> `createMemberRecordMock` IS called once -> `expect(createMemberRecordMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` FAILS. So the pin is non-vacuous: it flips outcome on deletion of the guard line. Caveat worth flagging: because `reset()` nulls `recordEditorMemberId` AND bumps generation together on every switch (:240 and the generation bump both fire unconditionally), this specific scenario can't isolate WHICH half of the `||` a future edit removed — deleting either clause alone still leaves the other clause catching this exact race. The pin proves 'the guard line as a whole must keep existing here,' which is what the issue actually asks for ('nothing defers the save's re-read and switches collective underneath it'), but does not prove both disjuncts are independently load-bearing.

findings.title: (6) #280 (4e5ebc8) did not touch this guard or its await — only shifted line numbers by +16
findings.detail: Diffed main:src/routes/roster/+page.svelte across 4e5ebc8: three hunks only, at old/new line pairs (1487->1487, 1560->1565, 1731->1747) — all inside `openRecordEditor`'s `state==='none'` prefill branch (adds `recordEditorOriginal = { ...recordForm };` at what is now :1567) and a comment-only rewrite in `saveRecordEditor`'s update-path diff-baseline section (now around :1750s), for issue #280 ('an untouched prefill no longer overwrites another admin's record entry'). Directly diffed the guard's neighborhood before/after (`git show 4e5ebc8^:...` lines 1695-1712 vs `git show main:...` lines 1711-1728) — byte-identical. Confirmed the guard itself moved from :1708 (pre-#280) to :1724 (post-#280) purely from the +16 lines inserted earlier in the function/effect; `const fresh = await loadMemberRecord(...)` moved from :1702 to :1718 the same way. #280's actual change (capturing the PREFILL as `recordEditorOriginal` baseline, and widening a comment) is orthogonal to the race guard and does not affect the pin's correctness — only its line-number citations, which this report already gives as current (:1704 g-capture, :1718 await, :1724 guard).

findings.title: (1) Visibility condition — component and caller, quoted (file:line)
findings.detail:
Component gate: src/lib/components/agenda/RepertoireElement.svelte:553 — `{#if pickableEditions.length > 0}`, wrapping the `<select data-testid="work-manage-add-programme-select">` at :554-566. The outer wrapper `data-testid="work-manage-add-programme"` (:552) is NOT gated on this — it's gated only on `canManageProgramme` (:551) — confirmed by RepertoireElement.programme-control.spec.ts:145-156, which pins the wrapper present with an empty pickable list. Prop default: RepertoireElement.svelte:219 `pickableEditions = []`.

Caller (agenda page): src/lib/components/agenda/AgendaList.svelte:347 — `pickableEditions={worksManage?.pickableEditionsByEventId[item.id] ?? NO_OPTIONS}`. That map is `pickableEditionsByEventId`, a `$derived.by` at src/routes/+page.svelte:1795-1817, built from `libraryWorks`/`libraryEditions` (read at :1801-1802, and :1766 for the sibling `editionsByWorkId`).

Working tree was on branch fix/299-create-path-collective-switch-guards, but `git rev-parse main HEAD` returned identical SHAs (e6fab8b) at the time of this check — no divergence yet — so the working-tree read is a main read; all line numbers are current, not stale.

A second caller with an identical construct exists on the event-detail page: src/routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte:1444 `pickableEditionsList = $derived.by(...)`, fed by its own `libraryWorks`/`libraryEditions` (declared :252-253), rendered into the same RepertoireElement at :3085. Issue #288 names only the agenda page's caller; the event-detail page is not mentioned in the issue. [speculative: whether a fix is meant to cover this second surface too — not stated in #288.]

findings.title: (2) No loading-vs-empty distinction exists today — verified: the caller genuinely cannot tell them apart
findings.detail:
`libraryWorks`/`libraryEditions` are declared as plain `$state<Work[]>([])` / `$state<Edition[]>([])` (+page.svelte:380-381; event/[id]/+page.svelte:252-253) — no nullable wrapper, no sibling loading/loaded boolean, nothing in the `WorksManage` interface (src/lib/repertoire/types.ts:88-104) beyond the raw `pickableEditionsByEventId: Record<string, PickerOption[]>` (types.ts:96-97). There is no route-load state machine either — `loadForSelected` is a plain async function, not backed by a `load()`/streaming or a status enum.

The vanish mechanics, confirmed by reading the code: `resetManagement()` (+page.svelte:1075-1090) sets `libraryWorks = []; libraryEditions = [];` synchronously, and its own comment (:1083-1090) states it "runs on EVERY `loadForSelected`, including the panel-preserving `{ keepSeasonManage: true }` reloads". Inside `loadForSelected` (:638-712), `resetManagement()` is called unconditionally at :703, regardless of `keepSeasonManage`. The refill is asynchronous and happens LATER, and — critically — after the point where the agenda itself has already finished rendering: `agendaLoading = false` is set at :786, inside the `.then()` of `loadFullAgenda()`, while `loadWorksAndManagement(worksCfg, eventIds, seasonId, thisRequest)` (which triggers `loadManagePickers` → the `listWorks`/`listAllEditions` fetch that eventually sets `libraryWorks`/`libraryEditions`, at :1271-1287) is called LATER in that same `.then()` block (around :830). So `agendaLoading` turning false does NOT mean the pickers have loaded — it turns false strictly before the picker fetch even starts. `agendaLoading` is therefore not usable, as-is, to distinguish "library not yet loaded" from "library loaded and empty" for this control; it answers a different, earlier-resolving question (has the agenda list itself loaded). This confirms the issue's claim: the caller currently has no state that distinguishes "not yet loaded" from "loaded and empty" for `libraryWorks`/`libraryEditions`.

What would have to be added, minimally: a boolean (or richer status) tracking specifically the `loadManagePickers`/`loadWorksAndManagement` picker fetch's own in-flight/settled state — set true when that fetch starts, false when it resolves/rejects — threaded through `WorksManage` (types.ts) → `AgendaList.svelte` (:347 area) → `RepertoireElement` as a new prop, so the component's gate can distinguish still-loading from loaded-and-empty rather than collapsing both to `.length === 0`. The event-detail page (event/[id]/+page.svelte) would need the identical addition if it is to get the same fix, since it has its own separate `libraryWorks`/`libraryEditions`/reset (`resetComposeState`, :415-422) with the same gap.

findings.title: (3) Precedent in neighbouring code: separate boolean load-state prop, not null-vs-[] on the data itself
findings.detail:
The codebase has a directly analogous precedent one screen away: the season-summary loader. `+page.svelte` declares `seasonRatesLoaded` (:431), `seasonRatesLoading` (:437), and `seasonRatesError` (:438) as three SEPARATE booleans alongside the data array `seasonMemberRates` (which itself stays a plain array, default `[]`, never null). The loader function (:2160-2198) guards re-fetch on `if (seasonRatesLoaded) return;` (:2164), sets `seasonRatesLoading = true` before the fetch (:2168) and `seasonRatesLoaded = true; seasonRatesLoading = false;` on success (:2191-2192), `seasonRatesLoading = false; seasonRatesError = true;` on failure (:2196-2197). These are passed straight through as two child props: `<SeasonSummary ... loading={seasonRatesLoading} error={seasonRatesError} ... />` (+page.svelte:7894-7897) — a dedicated `loading`/`error` prop pair on the consuming component, decoupled from the data prop.

A second, related-but-distinct precedent is the roster cache: `rosterCache` (:466) and `sectionsCache` (:541) are typed `{...} | null`, defaulting to `null`, where null means "not fetched" and a populated object means "fetched" (with a TTL) — but note this null-vs-object distinction lives on a separate CACHE field, not on the rows array itself; `rosterRows`/`rosterSections` (the arrays actually rendered) stay plain arrays with `[]` defaults, exactly like `libraryWorks`/`libraryEditions` today.

Taken together, the codebase's own convention for "can this consumer tell not-yet-loaded apart from loaded-and-empty" is a SEPARATE boolean flag (or flag pair) sitting beside the data, not a `null` vs `[]` reinterpretation of the data prop itself. That favours adding a separate load-state prop (e.g. per-event `pickableEditionsLoaded`/`pickableEditionsLoading`, or a page-level `picklistLoading`) over changing `pickableEditions`'s type to `PickerOption[] | null`, to stay consistent with `seasonRatesLoaded`/`seasonRatesLoading` and avoid an `?? []`-style call site regressing to the same ambiguity a nullable would introduce at every consumption point (`.length`, `.map`, etc. all need `?? []` again downstream, re-creating the same collapse this bug is about). [speculative: this is a design recommendation drawn from precedent, not a ruling — the actual choice is the team's/PO's call, per the issue's own framing of item 2 as a scope question and item 1 as needing "a load-state the component can see" without specifying its shape.]

findings.title: (4) Every existing spec asserting on this control's presence/absence
findings.detail:
Grep for `work-manage-add-programme` across the tree (testids used, not stale line numbers, per the issue's own warning):

- RepertoireElement.programme-control.spec.ts — the primary #272 RED spec. Directly asserts the empty→hidden / non-empty→shown gate: 'pickableEditions EMPTY → NO select and NO button; the wrapper itself stays' and 'pickableEditions non-empty → the select renders...', plus a same-shape 'FIRST-program_item fence' case with an empty list. These assert purely against the `pickableEditions` prop the component is handed directly (no page-level async timing) — a load-state fix that only changes the PAGE-LEVEL caller's derivation (not the component's own `.length > 0` gate or its default-prop behaviour) would not by itself break these; it would break them only if the component's own prop surface/default also changes and these call sites don't account for it.
- RepertoireElement.spec.ts — several tests pass `pickableEditions: [...]` non-empty and assert select/button wiring (ordinal-picking, per-surface rights checks asserting the wrapper is null for a season-only editor / no rights). Rights-gating assertions on the outer wrapper, orthogonal to load-state.
- RepertoireElement.ux.spec.ts — asserts the select IS present and is a native `<select>` with expected Tailwind classes, given a non-empty `pickableEditions`.
- page.repertoire-manage-wiring.spec.ts — page-level (through the real agenda page), the most load-timing-sensitive file: several tests use `await vi.waitFor(() => expect(...select...).not.toBeNull())` to await the SELECT appearing only after the async picker fetch resolves — i.e. they currently exercise (and implicitly rely on) the exact 'hidden while loading, appears once loaded' behaviour the issue flags as a fault on RELOAD. A load-state fix must keep these passing: first-render hidden→shown-on-load is explicitly stated by the PO ruling as unaffected ('First render is unaffected'). Also contains `installEditionlessWorld` tests asserting that once the edition fetch resolves to genuinely empty, the select/button STAY absent ('empty pickable list → a placeholder-only dropdown must not render') — this is the case that must still hide after the fix (loaded-and-empty), distinguishing it from the loading case.
- page.repertoire-ux.spec.ts — asserts the select renders (via `renderExpandedAsEditor()`) with expected classes.
- page.repertoire-a11y.spec.ts — the label-in-name guard spec (item 2 of #288), uses a non-empty `pickableEditions: [{ id: 'ed-new', ... }]` fixture; unrelated to load-state but shares the same testid surface.
- event/[id]/page.spec.ts — page-level for the event-detail page's OWN caller (its own `libraryWorks`/`libraryEditions`, per finding 1). One test asserts the wrapper present for a programmed event with an event-editor; another explicitly comments that the select node itself is re-derived when data lands and must be re-queried after `waitFor`, confirming this page has the identical load-then-appear dynamic as the agenda page.

Net: the component-level specs mostly pass `pickableEditions` directly and are insulated from a page-only load-state fix unless the component's own prop surface/gate changes; the page-level specs already tolerate an async appear-after-load window via `vi.waitFor` and would need re-checking against whatever new behaviour is introduced for the RELOAD-while-visible case specifically — none of the specs found currently simulate 'control already visible, then a same-collective reload happens' (see finding 5).

findings.title: (5) Reload while the control is already visible: many paths besides a collective switch — verified from code
findings.detail:
`resetManagement()` (+page.svelte:1075) is called unconditionally inside `loadForSelected()` at :703, on EVERY invocation, INCLUDING calls with `{ keepSeasonManage: true }` (the panel-preserving reload) — the function's own comment (:1083-1090) says exactly this. `loadForSelected()` is called from the actual collective-switch effect at :5675-5678 (`$effect(() => { selected; untrack(() => loadForSelected()); })`), but ALSO, with `keepSeasonManage` variously true or false, from many other same-collective write-completion paths:
- season create success: `loadForSelected()` at :2441
- season delete success: `loadForSelected()` at :3940
- season-manage-panel delete refresh: `loadForSelected({ keepSeasonManage: true })` at :3864 (`refreshAfterSeasonManageDelete`)
- event-convert bulk generate, failure/resume path: `loadForSelected({ keepSeasonManage: true })` at :4385
- event-convert bulk generate, success path: `loadForSelected({ keepSeasonManage: true })` at :4398
- event create success: `loadForSelected({ keepSeasonManage: origin === 'panel' })` at :4561 — `keepSeasonManage` is only true when the create originated from the panel, false otherwise, but `resetManagement()` fires either way
- series create bulk, failure/resume path: `loadForSelected({ keepSeasonManage: true })` at :5606
- series create bulk, success path: `loadForSelected({ keepSeasonManage: true })` at :5636
- `retryAgenda()`: `loadForSelected({ keepSeasonManage: eventConvertRunUnfinished })` at :5682 — an explicit user-initiated retry of the SAME collective's agenda, not a switch

Every one of these re-enters `loadForSelected`'s non-empty branch, which runs `resetManagement()` (blanking `libraryWorks`/`libraryEditions` synchronously) and then re-triggers `loadWorksAndManagement`/`loadManagePickers` asynchronously — the same vanish-then-reappear window the issue describes for a collective switch, reachable while the operator is mid-session on the SAME collective (e.g. just created a season, just deleted an event, just retried a flaky agenda load) with the control already visible and populated a moment before. So: yes — a reload while visible can happen via season create, season delete, the season-manage-panel's own delete refresh, event conversion (both success and failure/resume branches), event create, series bulk create (both branches), and an explicit agenda retry — none of these are a 'collective switch' in the sense of `selected` changing. The event-detail page has the analogous `resetComposeState()` (event/[id]/+page.svelte:415-422) with its own set of reload triggers, not enumerated here since #288 as filed is scoped to the agenda page.

findings.title: (1) The guard, its comment, and the pairing algorithm — verified at current lines
findings.detail:
File: src/routes/page.repertoire-a11y.spec.ts (read via `git show main:...`).

Comment (308-312): "// An aria-label key names its visible sibling by convention: strip `_aria_label` and the base (or base + `_button`) is the visible key. Keys with no such sibling (selects, the badge, the domain-texted external links) label controls with no visible text of their own — nothing to contain, so they're skipped here."

Guard `it(...)` block starts at line 307: "every aria-label whose control has visible text CONTAINS that visible text verbatim, in all four locales (WCAG 2.5.3)".

Pairing algorithm (314-321): collect every `repertoire_*_aria_label` key from en.json; for each, strip the `_aria_label` suffix to get `base`; look up `base` or `base + '_button'` in en.json; if neither exists, the key is dropped (`visibleKey ? {...} : null`, then filtered). Only surviving pairs (324-341) get the per-locale substring check (`aria.includes(visible)` on every variant pattern) run for en/et/lv/uk, each failure reported by locale.

So the guard's scope is defined by TWO independent filters: key prefix (`repertoire_`) and key suffix (`_aria_label`) on the aria-label side, AND a naming-convention match (`base`/`base_button`) on the visible side. A key can be dropped by convention-mismatch alone even when a real visible sibling exists under a different name — which is exactly what happens to the three select aria-labels below.

findings.title: (2) Full app enumeration — 26 <select> elements found, classified
findings.detail:
Searched every .svelte file in main (`git ls-tree -r main | grep .svelte$`) for `<select`. 26 real `<select>` elements across 10 files. Classified by what they render with NOTHING chosen:

PLACEHOLDER-PROMPT DEFAULT (shows an authored prompt string, not a value, until something is picked):
- RepertoireElement.svelte:357 `work-edition-picker`, aria-label `repertoire_pin_edition_select_aria_label` (:361), default option text `repertoire_pin_edition_label` (:364, "Pin edition"/"Vali trükiväljaanne"). Switches to showing the pinned edition's name once one is picked.
- RepertoireElement.svelte:521 `work-manage-add-work-select`, aria-label `repertoire_add_work_select_aria_label` (:525), default text `repertoire_add_work_label` (:528, "Add a work"/"Lisa teos"). Switches to the picked work's label once chosen.
- RepertoireElement.svelte:555 `work-manage-add-programme-select`, aria-label `repertoire_add_programme_select_aria_label` (:559), default text `repertoire_add_programme_label` (:562, "Select edition"/"Vali väljaanne") — this is the select the issue names. Switches to the picked edition's label once chosen.
- src/routes/+page.svelte:6296 `season-manage-conductor-select`, :7294 `season-create-conductor-select`, src/routes/admin/+page.svelte:653 `admin-add-admin-select`, :735 `admin-add-librarian-select`, +page.svelte:7672 `event-create-conductor-select` — all five are the same "picker" idiom (value forced back to `''` in the onchange handler itself, `<option value="" disabled selected hidden>` carrying `pickerPromptText(...)`). These NEVER show a value — 100% placeholder, always. aria-label keys (`season_conductor_label`, `admin_roles_add_admin_label`, `admin_roles_add_librarian_label`) are `_label`-suffixed, not `_aria_label`, and not `repertoire_`-prefixed — outside the guard's current key filter on both axes.
- src/routes/library/+page.svelte:1089 `bulk-checkout-work-select`, :1096 `bulk-checkout-edition-select`, :1507 `inline-checkout-{copy.id}` — placeholder default, but the aria-label attribute reuses the SAME message key as the placeholder option text (e.g. `aria-label={m.library_bulk_checkout_work_placeholder()}` and `<option value="">{m.library_bulk_checkout_work_placeholder()}</option>`), so these are already trivially compliant (identical string contains itself). Different prefix (`library_`) and suffix (`_placeholder`, not `_aria_label`) — outside guard's filter, but a working existing pattern worth citing in item 4.

VALUE-ONLY / NEVER-BLANK DEFAULT (no placeholder option exists at all; first render already shows a real, meaningful option):
- src/lib/components/profile/+page.svelte:944 `profile-time-format` (24h/ampm), :984 `profile-roster-names` (profile/real) — labeled by wrapping `<label for=...>`, no aria-label.
- src/routes/+page.svelte:6410 `series-create-type`, :6495 `series-create-repeat`, :7417 `event-create-type`... wait see event-create-type below — labeled by wrapping `<label>`, explicit comment at +page.svelte:6401-6403: "a never-blank <select> has no placeholder to name itself with, so the visible name is a wrapping <label>." No aria-label attribute.
- src/routes/+page.svelte:7437 `event-create-season`, :7455 `event-create-series` — also wrapping-`<label>`-named, though `event-create-series` DOES have a placeholder-shaped first option (`m.event_create_series_none()`, meaning "no series") — but again no aria-label, so moot for this guard.
- src/routes/+page.svelte:7417 `event-create-type` — HAS a placeholder option (`event_create_type_placeholder`) but explicit comment at 7412-7414 says a same-key aria-label was deliberately dropped as a redundant second name; wrapping `<label>` is the sole accessible name. No aria-label attribute exists to check.
- src/lib/components/TimeSelect.svelte:161/176/192 (hour/minute/ampm) — aria-label present (`time_select_hour_label` etc.) but the empty-state option renders truly blank text (`<option value={opt}>{opt}</option>` where `opt === ''`), not a message-keyed placeholder string. No distinct placeholder text exists to contain.
- src/routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte:2234 `event-edit-input-event_type` — aria-label `event_edit_event_type_aria_label` present, but the empty option is literally `<option value=""></option>` (blank), matching the guard's original stated rationale exactly ("no visible text of its own — nothing to contain").
- src/lib/components/admin/InviteSurface.svelte:390 `invite-db` — no aria-label (labeled by wrapping `<label>`); default option text is a hardcoded em-dash `"—"`, not a translatable placeholder at all.
- src/routes/+page.svelte:6516 `series-create-day` — has a placeholder option (`series_create_day_placeholder`) but no aria-label (wrapping `<label>` names it); moot for this guard.

All numbers verified against `git show main:<path>` this turn (git checked to confirm origin points to mvox-app.git before reading).

findings.title: (3) Accessible-name-contains-placeholder check, for the 3 selects the guard's own filter can actually reach
findings.detail:
Only three `repertoire_*_select_aria_label` keys exist, and per the enumeration above all three are placeholder-default selects — so under the ruling, all three are the ones actually in scope for THIS guard (the guard only ever scans `repertoire_`-prefixed, `_aria_label`-suffixed keys; the other placeholder-default selects found in part 2 use different key prefixes/suffixes entirely and are not reachable by this guard regardless of the ruling). Checked programmatically against all four locale files (`git show main:messages/{en,et,lv,uk}.json`):

- `repertoire_pin_edition_select_aria_label` vs `repertoire_pin_edition_label`: en 'Edition to pin for {work}' vs 'Pin edition' — NOT contained. et 'Trükiväljaanne teosele {work}' vs 'Vali trükiväljaanne' — NOT contained. Same for lv, uk. 4/4 locales fail.

findings.title: (4) What the guard change looks like mechanically
findings.detail:
Two independent gaps have to close, and they are separable:

A) Pairing-convention gap — the three select aria-label keys strip to bases (`repertoire_pin_edition_select`, `repertoire_add_work_select`, `repertoire_add_programme_select`) that don't exist; the actual visible/placeholder keys drop the `_select` infix (`repertoire_pin_edition_label`, `repertoire_add_work_label`, `repertoire_add_programme_label`). The cheapest fix is a code-only change to the pairing step (page.repertoire-a11y.spec.ts:316-320): when `base` ends in `_select`, also try the base with that trailing `_select` stripped (and its `_button` variant) as a fallback candidate before giving up. This needs no message-file renames and matches the naming this codebase already produced organically. (An alternative — renaming the three visible keys to `_select`/`_select_button` shape — costs the same 3-keys×4-locales edit as fixing the content below, for no benefit; not recommended.)

B) Content gap — regardless of A, the actual English/Estonian/Latvian/Ukrainian aria-label strings for these three keys don't contain their placeholder text (see item 3) and have to be rewritten so they do, in all four locale files (12 string edits total). The library page's existing pattern (`aria-label` reusing the exact same key as the placeholder option, e.g. `library_bulk_checkout_work_placeholder` used for both) is the cheapest content shape and already lives in this codebase — worth citing to whoever implements, though the repertoire selects carry a `{work}` parameter (pin_edition) that a bare shared-key reuse can't express, so at minimum `repertoire_add_work_select_aria_label` and `repertoire_add_programme_select_aria_label` could collapse to reusing their placeholder key directly; `repertoire_pin_edition_select_aria_label` needs its own string still containing `repertoire_pin_edition_label`'s text since it also carries `{work}`.

Per the team lead's ruling (issue #288, Palestrina's comment), the excluded-vs-included boundary itself should move out of the `:308-312` comment and into the guard's own assertion/failure message, since a boundary that lives only in a comment is exactly how the prior wrong generalization ("selects are excluded") took hold.

findings.title: (5) Genuinely ambiguous classification: the section-parent selects' 'Top level' default
findings.detail: src/lib/sections/SectionPicker.svelte:481 (`section-create-parent`) and src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:4999 (`roster-new-section-parent`) both default to `<option value="">{m.roster_new_section_top_level()}</option>` ("Top level"/"(top level)"). Unlike the three repertoire selects above, this string is not a pure imperative prompt that vanishes once any real choice is made — "Top level" is ALSO a legitimate, submittable final answer (it means "give this section no parent"), and a user who wants exactly that leaves it selected and submits. It simultaneously plays the role the ruling calls a placeholder (default, unchosen state) and the role it calls a value (a coherent, intentional answer, not an instruction to pick something else). I did not force this into either bucket — flagging it as the one case in the enumeration where the ruling's placeholder-vs-value line doesn't cleanly cut. (Moot for this guard's literal filter either way: aria-label key is `roster_section_parent_label`, not `repertoire_`-prefixed nor `_aria_label`-suffixed, so it's unreachable by the current guard regardless of how the ambiguity resolves — relevant only if the ruling's boundary is ever generalized beyond the repertoire_ prefix.)

findings.title: (6) Scope fence — what a switch-time clear alongside the reset callback would touch
findings.detail:
The natural placement, given the done-when's "the $effect chain is not the clearing mechanism" constraint, is three added lines inside the existing `reset: () => {...}` callback at `:313-319` (which already runs unconditionally on every (re)selection per `:303-306`'s comment) — setting `bulkCheckoutWorkId=''`, `bulkCheckoutEditionId=''`, `bulkCheckoutCheckedMembers=new Set()` there. This touches only that one callback body; the two `$effect`s at `:779-789` are untouched, matching the issue's "not in scope" instruction.

One interaction worth flagging for whoever implements it: the callback would run in the same synchronous tick as `selected` changing, before `works` has been refetched for the new collective. The unrelated auto-select `$effect` at `:772-777` (`if (works.length === 1) bulkCheckoutWorkId = works[0].id`) will subsequently re-fire once the new collective's `works` array populates (reset already having zeroed `bulkCheckoutWorkId`, so this is a fresh assignment, not a no-op-skip). If the new collective happens to have exactly one work, `bulkCheckoutWorkId` will be immediately repopulated with that (correct, new-collective) work id — which is the pre-existing #74 behavior, not a regression, but it means the cleared state does not necessarily stay empty; it becomes correctly-scoped instead, which is what's wanted. Setting all three fields directly in `reset()` rather than only `bulkCheckoutWorkId` also avoids relying on that cascade to zero the other two, which matters because `reset()` fires synchronously while `works` is still the old array for one tick — the two `$effect`s would otherwise be reacting to a still-stale `works.length` before the reload.
